newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai maize and soymeal firm amid limited supply.
newsitem.headline: Thai maize and soymeal firm amid limited supply.

text.p: Maize and soymeal prices rose further in Thailand this week as limited supply offset the impact of a slow market.
Traders said on Thursday some players were sidelined amid news the government was considering lifting the import quota and reducing import tariffs on certain animal feed ingredients.
The price of benchmark 14.50 percent-moisture maize paid by feed producers rose to around 4.50-4.60 baht a kg from 4.28-4.40 baht a week ago.
"It's the same old reason. Lots of maize was left dampened by rain in the farms. Little was transported to the market," one trader said.
The price of locally crushed soymeal from imported beans firmed to 10.20 baht from 10.05 last week.
Traders expected local prices to ease next month when soymeal from Brazil and Argentina arrived.

Thai feed millers recently ordered 36,000 tonnes of 44 percent protein soymeal from Argentina for prompt shipment. The price was said to be around US$306-307 per tonne C&F Bangkok, according to sources.
The cargo was expected to arrive in mid-October
